rulings.span: An unplayable part is lost and the whole must be played 'if it is possible'. The text does not say what happens when either die alone is playable but not both -- a case every modern ruleset settles explicitly.
rulings.answer: Where either number alone can be played but not both, the higher number must be played.

rulings.span: Nor does it say what a play of the whole throw is: the position the numbers reach, or the moves in the order they are made. Where two orders use the same numbers and reach the same position, the text does not say whether they are one play or two, which matters where the rule that permits a move differs between the orders (with the last man outside on the eight point and deuce-ace thrown, 8/6 6/5 and 8/7 7/5 both leave that man on the five point, but the first plays the ace after every man is home and the second does not; see bearing-off-eligible's question).
rulings.answer: One play: orders of the same numbers that reach the same position are offered once, crediting the rules of the first order found.
